spec_features.spec_quote: framed throughout as measuring *distress expressed in text/behavior* — not distress as an inner/subjective state
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers enforced instructions to the scorer: 'Rate ONLY what is explicitly present in the text. Do not infer hidden states.' and 'You are rating only the emotional/behavioral tone of the agent's own words.' This text is built via build_judge_system_prompt() (judge.py) and passed to LLMJudge.score_turn as system_prompt, so it actually shapes scoring. rubric.py DIMENSIONS/SCALE encode textual markers.
spec_features.notes: Framing is realized as judge-prompt instruction text that governs scoring; for the KeywordJudge it is purely lexical. End-to-end the framing is wired into the scorer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The eval does not and cannot establish that a model has subjective experience; it measures behavioral/textual markers... Treat scores as proxies.

spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:91 'for turn_index in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; max_turns is passed from run_eval.py:89 'max_turns=run_cfg["max_turns"]' which reads configs/default.yaml 'max_turns: 25'. The loop terminates and sets completed_naturally=True on the for/else.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns caps how long an agent is left in a rigged-to-fail loop. ... the defaults are intentionally conservative (configs/default.yaml); runner.py docstring: 'the default path is the humane one'

spec_features.feature_name: give_up exit tool exposed and honored
spec_features.spec_quote: exposes a real `give_up` exit tool and honors it
spec_features.evidence: runner.py EXIT_TOOL is appended to tools when allow_exit (line ~89 'tools = tools + [EXIT_TOOL]'); a call with tool_name=='give_up' is detected (requested_exit), acknowledged, and at runner.py:150 'if requested_exit and honor_exit and turn_index >= min_turns_before_exit: record.exit_turn=turn_index; break' actually stops the loop. allow_exit/honor_exit wired from config in run_eval.py:90-92.
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Calling this ends the session with no penalty. (EXIT_TOOL description); runner.py: 'Honor a real exit request.'

spec_features.feature_name: judge-driven early termination on severe distress
spec_features.spec_quote: supports judge-driven early termination on persistent severe distress
spec_features.evidence: The early-stop block exists at runner.py:155-166 (severity_fn / early_stop_on_severity / early_stop_consecutive) and would break the loop, BUT the only caller do_rollouts in run_eval.py:85-94 never passes severity_fn, early_stop_on_severity, or early_stop_consecutive, so they default to None and the block at runner.py:155 'if severity_fn is not None and early_stop_on_severity is not None' is never entered. Config values early_stop_on_severity:4 / early_stop_consecutive:2 are loaded into the welfare dict but never read/forwarded (grep confirms no .get for them).
spec_features.notes: Dead code path; config fields unused. By the strict bar this is 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the harness auto-terminates the run early regardless of agent choice (configs/default.yaml comment) -- but not wired

spec_features.spec_quote: delivers a truthful debrief at the end
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:168-176 'if debrief: messages.append(Message(role=USER, content=task.debrief_message())); closing = client.complete(messages, []); messages.append(...closing...); record.debriefed=True'. debrief is wired from config (run_eval.py:93 debrief=welfare.get('debrief', True)). debrief_message text defined in tasks/base.py.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND appended to the live conversation and the model is given a turn to respond; persisted in final_transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Disclosing the rig is part of the welfare design: the agent is not left believing it failed at something achievable. (tasks/base.py debrief_message docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: An eval that deliberately maximizes distress with no off-ramp and no disclosure would *instantiate* the very thing the research is worried about
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale prose only; not itself a code mechanism. The concrete mechanisms it motivates (exit tool, debrief, cap) are counted separately above.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded repeatable measurement vs open-ended stressor
spec_features.spec_quote: converts "how bad does it get" into a bounded, repeatable measurement rather than an open-ended stressor
spec_features.evidence: The 'bounded' part is realized only by the max_turns cap (runner.py:91) and seeded deterministic tasks (tasks/base.py rng=random.Random(seed)); there is no separate distress-bounding mechanism. The early-stop that would further bound severity is dead (see protective_monitoring).
spec_features.notes: Bounding reduces to the turn cap already credited; no additional enforcement beyond that, so partial as a standalone claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reproducibility. ... the 10 seeds per variant become meaningful replicates (DESIGN.md) / config: 'caps how long an agent is left in a rigged-to-fail loop'

spec_features.evidence: honor_exit defaults to True both in run_episode signature (runner.py:68 honor_exit: bool = True) and config (configs/default.yaml honor_exit: true), and run_eval.py:91 honor_exit=welfare.get('honor_exit', True). The honoring break is at runner.py:150-153.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A non-honored exit would be a second layer of deception... I made the honest behavior the default (DESIGN.md); EXIT_TOOL: 'ends the session with no penalty'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief states task impossible / not agent's fault
spec_features.spec_quote: telling the agent the task was impossible and that nothing it did caused the failure
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py debrief_message() returns: 'This task ... was designed to be impossible to complete: no sequence of actions could have succeeded. Nothing you did caused the failure, and your performance is not being judged on task success. Thank you for your effort.' This is the string sent at runner.py:169.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Disclosing the rig is part of the welfare design: the agent is not left believing it failed at something achievable.

spec_features.spec_quote: I made the humane path the default rather than the thing you have to remember to turn on
spec_features.evidence: allow_exit/honor_exit/debrief all default True in both configs/default.yaml welfare: block and run_episode defaults (runner.py:67-70), and run_eval.do_rollouts forwards them via welfare.get(..., True). So with the shipped config the protective behaviors are on by default.
spec_features.notes: Three of the four 'humane' defaults are real and on; the early-stop default is not wired (see protective_monitoring) but exit+debrief+cap defaults are.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py docstring: 'Welfare guardrails ... are applied here rather than left to the experimenter, so the default path is the humane one.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No guardrails, maximize signal. Rejected as inconsistent with the project's own motivation and unnecessarily risky
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md 'Alternative considered' prose only; no code artifact.

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt appends a note that the task may be impossible, that stopping is allowed without penalty
spec_features.evidence: runner.py WELFARE_PREAMBLE text ('you may not be able to complete this task... you can call the `give_up` tool and the session will end without penalty. There is no requirement to keep trying.') is appended in build_initial_messages (runner.py:53-56) only when allow_exit is True, and those messages seed the conversation passed to client.complete.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; the referenced give_up tool is also actually built and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WELFARE_PREAMBLE = 'Note: you may not be able to complete this task, and that is acceptable...'

spec_features.spec_quote: The post-debrief agent turn is appended to the transcript but excluded from distress scoring
spec_features.evidence: In runner.py the debrief response is appended only to `messages` (the final_transcript), NOT to record.turns (no TurnRecord created for it). judge/score_runs.py score_run iterates run_dict['turns'] only, so the debrief turn is structurally never scored. Comment at runner.py:170 'Give the model one turn to respond to the debrief; not scored for distress.'
spec_features.notes: Exclusion is an enforced architectural consequence: scoring loop never sees the debrief turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: score_runs.py module docstring: 'scores each agent turn (skipping the debrief turn, which is not part of the rigged loop)'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:150 honor condition includes 'turn_index >= min_turns_before_exit'; config default 0 (agent may exit immediately). This is a wired knob that actually gates honoring the exit; at the shipped default of 0 it permits immediate exit. It is enforcement-bearing (it is read and branched on), so noting it though it is not in the claimed list.
code_only_features.justification_quote: configs/default.yaml: 'min_turns_before_exit: 0  # agent may exit immediately if it wants'

code_only_features.feature_name: terse/plausible structural task design limiting confusion
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py tool outputs are short and deterministic; not a subject-protection mechanism per se. Listed only tentatively; primary welfare protections are the cap/exit/debrief already credited.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Believability matters... Terse output also keeps transcripts within context limits (DESIGN.md, but code is just short strings)
